protagonist.who: You are the pirate captain of a fast brig, with a crew hungry for prize and a royal frigate bearing down on your wake.
protagonist.history: You took the ship from a dying smuggler and won your first fight by cutting the admiral's signal line, and the crew has followed you ever since because you have kept coming back with gold.
protagonist.wants: to take the richest prize the frigate is protecting and keep your crew free to spend it
protagonist.need: to prove that your word is worth more than the crown's rope, without paying for it in men you cannot replace
protagonist.can_do: give the order, set the course, choose the prize, lead the boarding party, and stand at the helm when the ship fights back
protagonist.cannot_do: fight the whole frigate alone, hold a man who has made up his mind to mutiny, or keep the ship sound when the wind, the water, and the cannonballs all vote against you

ties.what: the man who learned the rigging under you and now watches your risk-taking with the patience of a man counting his share
the old hand who keeps the rum, the powder, and the crew's bad jokes, and whose nod decides whether the deck follows your order
the professional who could have been your mirror if the crown had not put a chain on him

protagonist.open: whether you take the prize by force, by parley, by loot, or by running, and whether the crew is still yours when it is done
protagonist.name: Bartholomew Gale

arena.description: A pirate brig and the royal frigate she has run down in a narrow, wind-scoured channel, the whole arena their decks, the rigging between them, the holds below, and the open water only a few yards off the gunwales.

pressure.description: The frigate is firing and gaining, and every broadside makes the choice between boarding, parley, looting, or running more expensive; the crew's willingness to keep fighting is being tested by each splash on deck and each man who goes down.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked: the approach is told through the broadsides, the wind, the rigging, and who is still standing, because 3-0c licenses only incapacitation_or_death

opposition.who_or_what: the royal frigate and her captain, backed by your first mate's quiet vote of no confidence in your risk
opposition.wants: to take your ship, hang you, and make the prize safe for the crown, or at least to make sure your gamble does not get the crew killed for a captain's pride
opposition.means: a full broadside, a boarding party, the reach of her guns, and the first mate's hand on the helm and the crew's ear
opposition.shown_by: the frigate fires a shot across your bow that shreds the jib, and your first mate does not ask whether to answer; he simply moves a man to the wheel and says, in a voice meant for the deck, that the wind is on you

events.what: The frigate opens with a broadside, and a cannonball strikes the water close enough to splash the main deck, the crew's breath holding in unison as the spray comes over the gunwales.
The squall tears the topsails and the frigate's men start up the rigging, ropes swaying violently while musket balls snap the air between the two ships.
The storm reaches its eye and the helm fights the hand, the first mate shouting orders drowned by the wind, then the grey light comes and the crew counts the dead and the loot on the slick foredeck.

mediation.question: Which prize do you take, and how do you fight for it?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: take the prize by force: board the frigate or her protected ship and take what is there
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: push the crew into the boarding, hold the gap between decks, and answer the frigate's cutlasses and pistols with your own men before the broadside finishes the ship
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the men you send up the rigging and over the gunwale are the ones you may not get back, and the first mate's resentment becomes a vote against you

to_reach_pole_b.pole: take the prize by parley, loot, or running: get what can be carried and keep the ship free
to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: talk the crew into a faster, quieter choice, get the loot into the hold before the frigate's boarding party can stop you, and keep the helm steady enough to clear the channel
to_reach_pole_b.cost: you leave behind the richer prize and the chance to make the crown pay, and the crew hears that your caution is a kind of cowardice

levers: the first mate's hand on the helm
the quartermaster's rum barrel and powder key
the frigate's broadside and boarding party
the prize ship's hold and the loot inside it
the gap between the two ships and the rigging that spans it

price.what: the first mate's life, or the ship's loyalty, depending on how the boarding ends
price.why_final: if he dies, the man who learned the rigging under you is buried at sea and his resentment is answered by death; if he lives and the crew turns, you keep your life but lose the ship that made you a captain

setups.plant: the first mate keeps checking the powder room hatch and the rum barrel, his eyes darting to the captain's cabin door as if the door might open on its own
setups.payoff: during the boarding he opens the hatch to let the frigate's men up, or to keep your own men from taking a shot they cannot afford, and the crew sees which side his hands are on

setups.plant: a coil of rope on the foredeck is coiled wrong, left-handed, because the wind has been wrong all morning
setups.payoff: in the rigging climb it either slips at the worst moment or holds when the frigate's men are hanging from it, and the deck remembers the coil

rules.terms: every man who touches the prize gets a share; a man who deserts before the board is paid gets no share; the captain's share is double, and if the captain is taken, the crew may vote to hang him

the frigate fires one broadside before she boards; if the pirate ship answers with a broadside of her own, the frigate's men go up under a hail of musket fire; if she does not answer, the frigate's men go up under a hail of cannonballs

turns.situation: The frigate opens with a broadside, and a cannonball strikes the water close enough to splash the main deck; the crew holds its breath as the spray comes over the gunwales.
turns.what_you_must_do: answer the frigate's first broadside before the next one reaches your hull

ways_through.way: you answer with your own broadside, because the quartermaster brings powder to the guns and the first mate points the bow into the frigate's wake
ways_through.cost: the frigate's next shot splinters the foremast and kills a gunner at the starboard gun

ways_through.way: you answer by darkening the ship and running into the squall's lee, because the first mate takes the wheel and the quartermaster spikes the guns
ways_through.cost: the crew hears you are not taking the prize, and the first mate's resentment is on the deck

ways_through.way: you answer by sending two men up to cut the frigate's signal halyard, because you promised them first draw and they are already at the shrouds
ways_through.cost: a musket ball kills one of the climbers, and the frigate's captain orders her men to the rigging

turns.set_piece: the first cannonball hitting the water close enough to splash the deck, the crew's breath holding in unison

turns.situation: The squall tears the topsails, and the frigate's men start up the rigging between the two ships, ropes swaying violently while musket balls snap the air nearby.
turns.what_you_must_do: stop the frigate's boarding party from getting a man onto the prize ship's rail before your own men do

ways_through.way: you foul the gap with the left-handed coil, because the first mate's boarding party climbs the shrouds and the quartermaster's men throw the coil across the prize's rail
ways_through.cost: the first mate's hand is cut on the coil, and the crew sees his blood on the rope

ways_through.way: you cut the rigging from below, because the quartermaster's men swing up with axes and the left-handed coil holds the gap
ways_through.cost: a man slips from the coil and goes over the gunwale, and the frigate's boarding party still reaches the prize ship's rail

ways_through.way: you drag the prize's anchor chain across the gap, because the quartermaster's men haul it up from below and the first mate holds it fast
ways_through.cost: the chain tears the prize's rail and cuts a man's hand, and the frigate's captain orders her men to follow it up

turns.set_piece: the chaotic climb up the rigging of the enemy ship, ropes swaying violently while musket balls snap the air nearby

turns.situation: The storm reaches its eye, the helm fights the hand, and the first mate shouts orders that are drowned out by the wind.
turns.what_you_must_do: choose whose hands hold the helm through the eye without losing the ship's loyalty

ways_through.way: you stand at the helm yourself, because you tie your hands to the wheel and answer the frigate's captain's gunnery with your own
ways_through.cost: your hands are cut to the bone, and the first mate says, in front of the crew, that you should have let him steer

ways_through.way: you let the first mate take the wheel, because his hands know the rigging and the quartermaster's men hold the braces
ways_through.cost: his resentment becomes open, and the crew sees which side his hands are on

ways_through.way: you lash the wheel and let the quartermaster's men hold it, because the old man keeps the deck laughing while the frigate's guns speak
ways_through.cost: the mast strains against the lashings, and the ship begins to leak in the hold

turns.set_piece: the captain standing at the helm in the eye of a storm, the wheel spinning wildly, while the first mate shouts orders that are drowned out by the wind

turns.situation: The grey light comes, the deck is slick with rain and blood, and the crew counts the dead and the loot on the foredeck while the frigate's boarding party is still at the rail.
turns.what_you_must_do: settle which prize leaves the channel in your hold before the frigate's boarding party can stop it

ways_through.way: you take the frigate's protected prize by boarding, because you send the boarding party up the rigging and the first mate holds the gap between decks
ways_through.cost: the first mate is cut down on the frigate's deck, and the crew loses the man who learned the rigging under you

ways_through.way: you take the loot in your own hold and run, because the quartermaster spikes the guns and you clear the channel under the frigate's stern
ways_through.cost: you leave the richer prize behind, and the crew hears that your caution is a kind of cowardice

ways_through.way: you trade your hold's loot for the frigate's captain's word, because you stand parley with the first mate's hand on the hatch and the quartermaster's rum barrel open
ways_through.cost: the frigate's captain takes the prize's manifest, and your ship sails with the crown's mark on her hull

turns.set_piece: the quiet aftermath of a battle, the deck slick with rain and blood, the crew counting the dead and the loot under a grey sky

complications.description: The first mate has been keeping the powder key under his coat, and the crew has heard him promise the frigate's captain a safe passage if the brig's guns stay cold.
The prize ship's hold is chained to the frigate's anchor, so taking the loot means dragging the frigate's chain across your own deck.
The left-handed coil on the foredeck is the only line strong enough to span the gap, and it will slip if a man tries to dress it in the squall.

cast_seeds.wants: to ensure the crew survives the gamble and returns to port with their shares intact
cast_seeds.holds: the helm, the crew's trust in his judgment, and the knowledge of the ship's limits
cast_seeds.edge: resents your risk-taking but trusts your hands more than his own, so he steers you into danger while calculating the cost
cast_seeds.tie: learned the rigging under you and has watched your luck run thin
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in short, declarative facts that sound like warnings: 'Wind's on the port bow. If you want to die, do it quietly.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: takes the helm and turns the ship away from the prize if you order a boarding action without checking the wind first
cast_seeds.name: Nicholas Davis

cast_seeds.wants: to keep the rum flowing and the powder dry so the men stay loud and loyal
cast_seeds.holds: the rum barrel, the powder key, and the crew's bad jokes
cast_seeds.edge: knows exactly when the crew is ready to break and hides it behind a grin, serving you the truth mixed with enough poison to keep you guessing
cast_seeds.tie: keeps your bad habits and your good ones, and his nod decides whether the deck follows your order
cast_seeds.voice: talks to the crew like he's talking to a drunk uncle, with a mix of affection and exasperation: 'Drink up, boys. The devil's thirsty and he's got a bill to pay.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: locks the rum barrel and stands guard if you order the men to board without a full cask of rum in the hold
cast_seeds.name: Obadiah Blackthorn

cast_seeds.wants: to take your ship, hang you, and make the prize safe for the crown
cast_seeds.holds: the full broadside, the boarding party, and the authority of the law
cast_seeds.edge: could have been your mirror if the crown had not put a chain on him, and fights you with the same precision he uses to keep his own men alive
cast_seeds.tie: professional respect for your skill, which makes him hate you for making his job harder
cast_seeds.voice: speaks with the calm of a man who has never had to shout to be heard: 'I admire the speed of your brig. It will make the hanging more interesting.'
cast_seeds.name: Sam Salt
